belief: God took them from me to punish me.
origins: After a death, guilt over old sins or an unresolved conflict can lead us to wonder if God is repaying us. People of faith can add to this by saying things like “God needed another angel” or “everything happens for a reason,” which can make God sound like the cause of the loss and imply that we deserved it.
teaches: Paul writes, “There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” The psalmist says, “He has not dealt with us according to our sins or repaid us according to our iniquities.” When the disciples asked who sinned to cause a man’s suffering, Jesus said that it was not this man or his parents. Jeremiah’s lament says, “Even if He causes grief, He will show compassion.” And “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” Death entered the world through sin and brokenness in general, not as a personal tally against you. God grieves with you.
self_statements: I am being punished for my sin.
God took them because of what I did.
If I had been better, they would be here.
This is the price of my past.
errors: Believing the death was about me.
Linking my sin to a death.
Feeling guilty and concluding that God punished me.
questions: What do I believe I did, and have I confessed it?
Does Scripture teach that God kills loved ones to punish us?
What did Jesus say when asked whose sin caused suffering?
What does God’s love at the cross say about His attitude toward me?
Who said that God needed my loved one, and is that biblical?
What do I need to bring to God in honest prayer?
truth: God did not take my loved one to punish me. In Christ there is no condemnation, and Jesus rejected the idea that suffering is always payment for sin. God grieves with me, and I can bring my pain and any guilt to Him.
hw_truths: There is no condemnation in Christ.
God does not repay me according to my sins.
God proved His love at the cross.
log: Each time guilt rises, write Romans 8:1 and one truth about God’s compassion.
actions: Write what you think you are being punished for.
Bring any real sin to God and receive forgiveness.
See how Jesus answered the question.
Share your fear and ask for biblical perspective.
prayer: Lord, I have wondered if You took them because of me. Thank You that there is no condemnation in Christ. Forgive what needs forgiving, and comfort me with Your compassion. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I think I am being punished for?
What did Jesus say about suffering?
Who told me God needed them?
name_example: Sarah can write: “There is no condemnation for me in Christ, so this is not punishment.”
